content: Fructans are polymers composed of multiple fructose molecules. These compounds are naturally present in various foods, including artichokes, asparagus, green beans, leeks, onions (including spring onions), and wheat. In addition to their presence in human food, fructans are also found in grasses, which serve as animal fodder. This has dietary implications for animals such as horses and other members of the equidae family. In plants, fructans serve as a storage form of energy. Plants that store their energy as fructans exhibit an enhanced ability to survive in low-temperature environments. This is because fructans provide a protective mechanism against freezing by binding to cellular membranes, which helps maintain the structural integrity of the cells.
